Key Research Thinking Patterns: Unsupervised Contrastive Risk Stratification: Leveraging contrastive learning to group tissue samples by malignant transformation risk rather than binary classification, effectively reducing inter-patient variability and identifying high-risk clusters in oral potentially malignant diseases.

Patient-Invariant Multitask Representation Learning: Utilizing contrastive pre-training to create patient-invariant features, enabling a multitask framework that simultaneously performs cancer diagnosis and margin delineation while handling small datasets without paired healthy references.

Tissue-Specific Fairness-Aware Fine-Tuning: Identifying and mitigating algorithmic bias where tissue-type information is entangled with disease features, employing tissue-specific fine-tuning to disentangle these factors and reduce fairness gaps in diagnostic models.

Morphological-Enhanced Deep Transfer Learning: Integrating segmented mass contour information into pseudo-color image generation for mammography, providing complementary morphological features that significantly enhance the classification performance of deep learning models like VGG16.
Summary Description: Javier Jo specializes in biomedical engineering and medical artificial intelligence, focusing on non-invasive diagnostic tools for oral and breast cancers. His research integrates multispectral autofluorescence lifetime imaging (maFLIM) with advanced deep learning architectures to enable early detection, risk stratification, and surgical margin delineation. Key methodological contributions include unsupervised contrastive clustering for handling inter-patient variability, multitask learning for simultaneous diagnosis and segmentation, and fairness-aware fine-tuning to mitigate bias in clinical AI. He also develops hardware systems, such as handheld FLIM endoscopes, for label-free metabolic imaging. His work extends to computer-aided diagnosis in mammography, where he enhances deep learning performance through morphological feature integration, demonstrating a strong translational impact in improving clinical decision-making and equitable healthcare outcomes.
